SMTO-GML-0061 — Some chosen emails aren't in the folder you named

GUID: 737722d1-9c62-46f7-80c8-fbd2c8f21416
Slug: gmail-selection-scope-mismatch
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • SMTO was given specific emails to change, but at least one isn't in the folder the request was limited to, for example it's in Spam or Trash. SMTO stopped before changing any of them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check in Gmail where those emails are now: Inbox, Spam, Trash, or archived. The request stopped because at least one email isn't where the request said it would be.
  2. Ask SMTO again and name the folder to use: Inbox, Spam, Trash, or anywhere, which includes Spam and Trash. SMTO won't widen a request to Spam or Trash on its own.
  3. If the emails moved after you picked them, ask SMTO to search for them again before making the change. A fresh search uses each email's current folder.

What success looks like

  • SMTO accepts the selection, shows how many emails it will change, and the action finishes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't choose anywhere just to get past this unless you really mean to include Spam and Trash.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An explicit message_ids or thread_ids selection includes a message whose labels don't match the requested scope (inbox, trash and spam require that label; all_mail excludes SPAM and TRASH).

What this means

  • Explicit IDs are checked against their labels before writes. Normal All Mail excludes Spam and Trash; named folders require their corresponding label.

Why this can happen

  • Explicit IDs are checked against their labels before writes. Normal All Mail excludes Spam and Trash; named folders require their corresponding label.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the selected messages' labelIds and resubmit with the intended scope (inbox, trash, spam, all_mail or anywhere), or drop the mismatched IDs. The check in gmail/workflows.select runs before any write and never broadens all_mail.
  • Check the selected IDs and explicitly choose their intended scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the selected IDs and explicitly choose their intended scope.

How to verify the fix

  • All selected messages belong to the requested mailbox scope.

What not to do

  • Do not silently broaden normal All Mail to Spam, Trash or anywhere.

Technical notes

  • This check rejects new work before its write. It does not undo previous confirmed effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
